text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Cabinet portfolio swap said to be close.
- "We are all Aryeh Deri," chant supporters at rally.
- President Ezer Weizman calls on Shas leaders to bury the ethnic hatchet.
- Infrastructure Ministry: Land reform to be approved next week. Bar-On Affair makes ministers wary of minister Ariel Sharon's candidate to head Israel Lands Administration.
- Funds of U.S. investment magnate George Soros raise stake in El-Rov Israel Ltd.
GLOBES
- Rise of 9 percent in March comprehensive index.
- Morgan Stanley holds 7.88 percent of Supersol shares.
HAARETZ
- Pressures grow on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu within the government to remove justice minister from his job.
- Trial of Azam Azam, accused of spying for Israel, opens today in Cairo.
- North Korea supplied Iran with programme for making weapons capable of striking at Israel.
- Minority opinion in prosecution: To put Netanyahu, Hanegbi and Deri on trial -- or none of them.
MAARIV
- Weizman warns: "Don't let the ethnic genie out of the bottle."
- Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel will announce interest rate today -- no significant change expected.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- President: We mustn't let the ethnic genie out of the bottle.
- Prime minister asks Shin Bet security service for less protection.
